title: Design patterns at a glance
idea: A design pattern is a named, reusable shape of classes that solves a problem which keeps coming back, such as hiding which class gets created.
points: A pattern is a structure you adapt, not a library you import.
The Gang of Four book groups its patterns: creational, structural, behavioural.
A pattern name lets you say a design in one word to a reviewer.
Most patterns lean on an `interface` so a new class can plug in.

hero.caption: Name the problem first; the family narrows the pattern list to a few.

code.title: Factory and Decorator
code.caption: A factory picks the notifier; a decorator adds a tag without touching it.

walk.text: The shared contract both patterns rely on.
Factory pattern: callers ask by name and never see which implementation they get.
Decorator: it is a `Notifier` and also has one inside.
It adds its tag, then forwards the call to the wrapped object.
`main` mixes plain and decorated notifiers behind one type.

pitfalls: Do not start from a pattern and hunt for a problem; start from the problem.
Avoid stacking patterns for a feature that a plain method solves.
Name the pattern in the class or a comment so readers spot it.

quiz.why: The outer decorator adds `[a] ` and forwards. The inner one then puts `[b] ` in front of that text before the SMS notifier prints it.

takeaway: Patterns are named answers to recurring problems; start from the problem.
